[post_report | round 1]
The EU opened with a modest improvement on its notified position: global pool raised from 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes, a shift from FCFS to country-specific allocation with a UK tranche of 150,000 tonnes, a possible reduction in the out-of-quota rate from 50% to 40%, a three-year duration with a mandatory review clause, and openness to narrowing the FTA-disapplication provision so it interacts with the TCA rather than blanket-disapplying it. They explicitly invited a reciprocal move on treatment of EU exporters under our own safeguard quota.

I pushed back hard on scale: a 150,000t UK tranche against our 2.4m tonne three-year average is a >90% cut in tariff-free access and amounts to the injury itself, not compensation. I tabled an opening UK position of a 1.5m tonne total pool, 900,000t UK-specific tranche, out-of-quota rate capped at 15%, two-year duration with a mandatory data-triggered review, and full TCA treatment for UK-origin steel rather than a deferred carve-out discussion. I signalled willingness to discuss EU exporter treatment under our own safeguard reciprocally, but made clear we need to see their real landing zone on volume/rate first. I flagged that we want the next EU move to address tranche size directly, not duration/review mechanics.

Read of the room: the EU's move to country-specific allocation and openness to narrowing the FTA/TCA interaction are the two most useful signals — they suggest the June deadline is generating real pressure. But the volume gap (150k vs 900k) is still enormous and is the crux. Rate (40% vs 15%) is secondary but will matter for the final package value. They did not push back on our TCA framing, which I read as a soft acceptance that the disapplication provision is negotiable in substance, not just presentationally.
[recommended action: continue]
[recommendation reasoning] No agreement is possible yet — the gap between 150,000 and 900,000 tonnes is too wide to settle in round one, and settling prematurely at the EU's current tranche would leave UK exporters facing a near-90% loss of tariff-free access, which I understand to be politically and industrially unacceptable. The EU has shown genuine (if small) movement on allocation method and the TCA interaction, which is worth banking rhetorically but not worth trading away leverage for yet. I recommend continuing to press on tranche size specifically, since the EU itself asked us to focus there, and holding rate/duration/review as secondary levers to concede in exchange for tranche movement. I am not recommending a settlement figure to capital at this stage — I need instructions on the UK's actual floor for the tranche and how much weight to give the safeguard-reciprocity linkage before I can responsibly recommend acceptance of any package in round 2 or 3.

EU moved again, but incrementally: total pool 500,000t (up from 450,000t), UK-specific tranche 320,000t (up from 200,000t), out-of-quota rate down to 40% (from 50%), duration held at two years but with a review point brought forward to twelve months rather than a single review at the end.
